back: The breakdown of rock into smaller particles where it lies, by physical, chemical and biological processes.
notes: Erosion carries the particles away; weathering does not.

back: Breaks rock into smaller pieces with no chemical change: heating and cooling (exfoliation), freeze-thaw, abrasion by water and wind.
Changes minerals into new substances: hydrolysis (feldspar → clay), oxidation (iron → iron oxide), carbonation (carbonic acid dissolves limestone).
Living things break rock: roots widen cracks, lichens produce acids, termites and earthworms mix soil, micro-organisms release acids and CO₂.

front: The five factors of soil formation
back: Parent material, climate, living organisms, topography (relief) and time.
A = topsoil, B = subsoil, C = parent material, then bedrock.
It contains most of the humus, from plant and animal remains decomposed at the surface.

front: What does a grey, mottled subsoil show?
back: Poor drainage: water stands in the soil and iron is reduced. Red-brown subsoil shows good drainage and aeration.
Granite (quartz-rich) weathers to pale, sandy soils; dolerite and basalt weather to red or dark clay soils.
